title: Acyclicity of the pulled-back etale injectives
statement:
If $X$ is affine and $I$ is injective in etale module sheaves on $X$, then

$$
 H^q(U_{\Proet},(\nu_X^*I)|_U)=0
 \quad(U\in\mathcal B_X,\ q>0).
$$

Here the left side is derived evaluation on the basis object $U$.

proof.text: Put $M=\nu_X^*I$. The basis and Čech criterion reduce derived evaluation vanishing on every $U\in\mathcal B_X$ to positive Čech vanishing for every finite basis covering. For the empty covering, joint surjectivity forces $U=\varnothing$; each Čech group in positive degree is zero.

source.place: Tag 099U, first paragraph and empty-family case

proof.text: For a nonempty finite basis covering, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-intersection-limit-compatibility] gives finite affine étale coverings of the fixed target $U$, with face-compatible limits for all ordered intersections. The stages remain ind-étale over $X$.

source.place: Tag 099U, second paragraph, presentations and fibre products

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-basis-cech-first-limit], the Čech cohomology of the original covering is the filtered colimit of those stage covering cohomologies. It suffices to kill each stage group.

source.place: Tag 099U, second paragraph, first displayed Čech-colimit formula

proof.text: Fix a stage covering $\{W_a\to U\}$. Present $U=\varprojlim_iU_i$ by [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra], with directed indexing from [lem-weil-pbc-filtered-category-directed-cofinal]. Affine stages are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-etale-finite-cover-factorization-descent] with terminal target $W=U_{i_*}$ and terminal auxiliary objects: its covering models over $U_{i_0}$ pull back to the given family. Base change them for $i\ge i_0$. They cover by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]; their sources are affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine] and clauses (1)-(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence].

source.place: Tag 099U, second limit; descent as in etale-cohomology Tag 0EYL

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-cover-cech-stage-comparison] with $F=I$. Every stage family is a finite affine étale covering on $X_{\Et}$; [new-etale-finite-affine-cech-basis] checks the basis/intersection/refinement hypotheses. Injectivity of $I$ in the module category therefore gives zero positive Čech cohomology at every stage by the first clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion]. The second-limit comparison makes the fixed covering group zero. No injectivity of an underlying abelian sheaf or of $I|_U$ is used.

source.place: Tag 099U, final Čech-colimit formula and injective vanishing

proof.text: The first colimit is therefore zero for every finite basis covering. The second assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion] gives zero derived evaluation on every $U\in\mathcal B_X$.

Finally $U\to X$ is weakly étale by [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability], and [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-restriction-injectives] identifies derived evaluation with $H^q(U_{\Proet},M|_U)$. This is the claimed vanishing.

source.place: Tag 099U, restriction to the pro-étale slice

proof_origin.place: Tag 099U (lemma-affine-vanishing), full two-limit proof; constant-coefficient module version via lem-weil-pbc-cech-criterion

theorem isZero_rightDerived_sectionsFunctor_comparisonUpperStar_obj {U V : Scheme.{u}}
    (f : U ⟶ V) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f] (I : Sheaf U.smallEtaleTopology A)
    [Injective I] (W : V.AffineProEt) (q : ℕ) :
    IsZero (((sectionsFunctor A ((MorphismProperty.Over.pullback @WeaklyEtale ⊤ f).obj
      ((AffineProEt.toProEt V).obj W))).rightDerived (q + 1)).obj
        ((comparisonUpperStar A U).obj I))
lean.note: Existing upstream theorem, read both locally and through scompile.py --source. Specialize A to ModuleCat.{u+1} Λ, U=V=X, and f=𝟙 X. The canonical MorphismProperty.Over.pullbackId identifies the evaluation object X ×_X W with W, and NatTrans.rightDerived transports this natural evaluation isomorphism. QuasiCompact and QuasiSeparated of the identity are inferred, so no hypotheses on X beyond the node are added. The natural number q in the upstream declaration indexes degree q+1, exactly all positive degrees. Scheme.AffineProEt is the recorded ind-etale basis on affine X. This specialization, including the canonical identity transport, was compiled in a sandbox-only scratch check. The theorem applies to arbitrary Grothendieck abelian coefficients, hence in particular to left modules over the finite discrete coefficient ring used by the comparison adjunction. No new theorem or copied notion is delivered; the upstream theorem is not claimed sorry-free.
